title: Source Editor Image Presentation Delivery
summary: add caption, summary, and responsive image-placement authoring through one modular server-owned source fragment
content_html:
Source Editor Image Presentation Delivery

Status And Purpose

Completed as SIP-1 under Roadmap. All checkpoints and durable authority transfer are complete. This delivery remains available pending separate retirement confirmation.

SIP-1 extends the source editor's existing Add image… workflow with one consistent figure presentation. Caption, summary, and image placement stay in the Add image modal. A separate format chooser is deferred until more than one real fragment format exists.

Complete Outcome

An author can add a staged image and choose:

  • required image alt text;
  • the existing checked-by-default Add caption option;
  • independently editable caption text, initially suggested from the alt text;
  • optional short summary text; and
  • Full column, Image left, or Image right from one grouped placement control; and
  • a checked-by-default Fill available width option.

Unchecked Add caption preserves the current plain Markdown image insertion. When it is checked, the server returns one semantic <figure> / <figcaption> source fragment. Full-column presentation places the text below the image. Left and right presentation use equal visual columns for the image and text, then collapse to image followed by text on narrow screens.

The inserted source remains readable and manually editable. Existing authored images and caption spans are not migrated.

Fill available width enlarges the image to its available full or split column. When unchecked, the image retains its intrinsic width while remaining capped to its available column so it cannot overflow on narrower screens.

Text is aligned left or right so that it mirrors the image, as shown in the image below:

Image Alignment

Fragment Ownership

  • The browser sends semantic values only: alt text, caption, summary, one allowlisted placement value, and an explicit fill-width boolean. It does not send HTML, CSS classes, inline styles, or arbitrary dimensions.
  • A focused server module owns validation, escaping, and source-fragment generation. The staged-media service continues to own publication, preview/apply orchestration, and response shaping.
  • Preview and apply call the same fragment builder so the confirmed source is the source inserted after publication.
  • The initial module uses explicit small builder functions for plain images, figure images, and file links. It does not load template files or introduce a general template, registry, or plugin framework.
  • A future fragment may add another explicit builder and allowlisted format only when that format has a concrete user contract. The Add image modal gains no format selector in SIP-1; a separate format modal is considered only after multiple formats make it useful.
  • The portable Docs Viewer stylesheet owns figure layout and responsive behavior so Manage, public, and embedded-detail readers share one result. Management CSS owns only the modal controls.

Caption and summary are plain text in SIP-1. The server escapes both because the current trusted authored-content renderer permits raw HTML and does not sanitize generated source fragments.

Modal Contract

The existing Add image modal remains the only workflow surface.

  • Staged file and Alt text retain their current roles.
  • Add caption retains its current default.
  • When captioning is enabled, caption, summary, and placement controls are conditionally enabled in the same modal.
  • Caption begins with the suggested alt text but becomes independent once edited. It is required while Add caption is checked, and changing visible caption copy must not silently rewrite alt text.
  • Summary is optional supporting copy, not general document prose, and renders at the Docs Viewer caption size.
  • Full column means the complete Docs Viewer prose measure, not a viewport-bleed layout.
  • Image left and Image right describe visual placement. Source and accessible reading order remain image, caption, then summary.
  • Fill available width is checked by default. Unchecked images retain their intrinsic width, shrink only when needed to avoid overflow, and align with their selected presentation edge.
  • Add file… remains unchanged.

Boundary

In scope:

  • one semantic figure fragment;
  • modular code-owned fragment generation without template files;
  • caption text separate from alt text;
  • optional plain-text summary;
  • three fixed placement choices;
  • one fixed fill-width choice without custom dimensions;
  • equal-column desktop presentation and narrow-screen stacking;
  • server-side value validation and HTML escaping;
  • identical preview/apply fragments;
  • portable reader CSS; and
  • focused service, fragment, runtime-module, and manual visual evidence.

Not in scope:

  • a separate format modal or format selector;
  • a general fragment/template registry, schema-driven modal, or plugin system;
  • arbitrary HTML, Markdown summary, CSS classes, widths, alignment, or style input;
  • viewport-bleed, galleries, carousels, overlays, lightboxes, crop controls, focal points, or responsive source selection;
  • rewriting existing document source;
  • changing media storage, publication, collision, SVG sanitization, Mermaid, logical-token, or source-editor save behavior; or
  • any change to Add file….

Likely Authority

  • source-editor-media.js owns the Add image modal controls and semantic request values.
  • A focused docs_staged_media_fragments.py module owns fragment validation, escaping, and code-based builders.
  • docs_staged_media_service.py retains staged-media preview/apply and provider-independent publication.
  • site/docs-viewer/static/css/docs-viewer.css owns the portable figure component and responsive layout.
  • Existing staged-media Python tests own exact fragment and request behavior; a focused runtime-module check should protect semantic request projection without asserting ordinary modal choreography or visual layout.
  • Media And Asset Handling receives the durable extension method. Source Editor Endpoints receives only the shipped request/response fields.

Implementation may adjust filenames after inspection, but must retain these ownership boundaries.

Delivery Checkpoints

[x] SIP-1.0 — Fragment And Service Contract

  • [x] Add the focused code-owned fragment module with explicit plain-image, figure-image, and file-link builders.
  • [x] Validate caption, summary, and placement once and escape every generated HTML text or attribute boundary.
  • [x] Route preview and apply through the same builder while preserving plain unchecked images and all existing file behavior.
  • [x] Prove exact full-column, left, right, absent-summary, invalid-placement, and hostile-text output with pure/service tests.

Evidence:

  • docs_staged_media_fragments.py now owns the explicit plain-image, figure-image, and file-link builders. The figure builder maps only full, left, and right to fixed server-owned classes and emits readable image-first <figure> / <figcaption> source.
  • Caption and placement are explicit required plain-text request values when add_caption is true. Summary is optional plain text. HTML attributes and text nodes are escaped at generation, and invalid or absent semantic values fail before a source fragment is returned.
  • Both ordinary and Mermaid preview/apply payloads route through the same _source_fragment owner. Unchecked images retain plain Markdown and file links retain their existing Markdown path.
  • The two focused Python files pass 34 tests. Explicit four-file Python lint and bytecode compilation pass, and git diff --check passes.
  • The browser request and reader CSS are deliberately unchanged at this gate. Captioned Add image is not an end-to-end path until SIP-1.1 supplies the new required values. No old-request fallback or compatibility alias remains.

Stop for review of generated source shape and service boundaries before UI and CSS work.

[x] SIP-1.1 — Add Image Controls And Reader Presentation

  • [x] Keep caption, summary, and grouped placement controls in the existing Add image modal, with the checked-by-default fill-width option; do not add a format workflow.
  • [x] Pass semantic values through the current staged-media preview/apply request and insert only the returned server fragment.
  • [x] Add portable full-column and split figure styles with equal columns, caption-size text, and narrow-screen image-first stacking.
  • [x] Confirm current collision confirmation, dirty-buffer insertion, SVG and Mermaid paths, and Add file… remain unchanged.

Evidence:

  • The one existing Add image modal now keeps its checked-by-default caption toggle and conditionally enables caption, summary, and one three-radio placement group plus Fill available width, also checked by default. Alt text seeds caption until caption is edited; caption edits never project back into alt text.
  • Captioned preview/apply requests carry only caption, summary, allowlisted placement, and validated boolean fill_width values alongside the existing media request. An unchecked caption omits those fields, Add file carries none of them, and the editor still inserts only payload.markdown returned after publication.
  • Portable docs-viewer.css owns full-column and equal-column split figures. Image-left text aligns left, image-right text aligns right, and both split variants reset to image-first single-column, left-aligned content at the existing narrow-screen breakpoint. The public template and tracked public routes use the advanced docs-viewer-style-20260731a cache key.
  • Manual full-column review exposed collapsed summary line breaks. Summary normalization now preserves authored lines while still normalizing line endings and per-line whitespace; portable reader CSS renders them with white-space: pre-line.
  • Manual comparison with a pre-delivery 620-pixel image exposed that placement and enlargement were coupled. The modal now keeps Fill available width checked by default; unchecking it emits the fixed docsViewerFigure--natural-width modifier so the image keeps intrinsic width, remains capped to its column, and follows the existing responsive alignment.
  • The maintained Manage route smoke passes default fill, unchecked fill, unchecked caption, and file request projections. The 41 fragment/service tests pass, including raster, SVG, Mermaid, collision, and file-link coverage; 10 relevant static-asset tests pass. The unrelated package-action ownership assertion remains excluded after its current failure in unchanged runtime files.
  • Explicit JavaScript lint and syntax checks, focused smoke Python lint and bytecode compilation, site validation, and git diff --check pass.

Representative author review accepted the primary full/split, summary-line, and fill/natural-width results. This was not an exhaustive combination matrix.

[x] SIP-1.2 — Focused Verification And Authority Transfer

  • [x] Run fragment/service tests, explicit Python and JavaScript lint, the smallest route/module check that proves request wiring, and git diff --check.
  • [x] Inspect generated source plus rendered Manage, public, and embedded-detail examples without treating one visual sample as subsystem-wide evidence.
  • [x] Update the durable media extension method and exact staged-media endpoint contract from shipped behavior.
  • [x] Independently review the final diff for duplicated fragment ownership, unsafe interpolation, public/manage CSS drift, compatibility residue, and unplanned format machinery before changing status.

Evidence:

  • The focused closeout run passed 51 relevant tests: 41 fragment/service tests and 10 static-asset tests. The unrelated package-action ownership assertion remains explicitly deselected after its current failure in unchanged runtime files.
  • The Manage service route smoke passed default fill, unchecked fill, unchecked caption, Add file, collision, dirty-buffer insertion, and existing route boundaries. Its expected negative permission and absent-route probes remained 403 / 404 responses.
  • Explicit JavaScript and Python lint, JavaScript syntax, Python compilation, deploy-root validation, and git diff --check passed.
  • Generated figure source was inspected for both fill states. The portable site/docs-viewer/static/css/docs-viewer.css component remains the shared Manage, public, and embedded-detail presentation owner; management CSS owns only modal layout.
  • Media And Asset Handling now owns the shipped figure architecture and extension method. Source Editor Endpoints now owns the exact request, validation, fragment, and apply contract.
  • Final diff review found one explicit fragment builder and class map, one service handoff, escaped server-owned HTML, strict boolean and placement validation, and no compatibility path, arbitrary style input, format modal, template registry, or duplicate public/manage figure CSS.

Completion Evidence

SIP-1 completed on 2026-07-31 with:

  • [x] unchecked images still insert ordinary Markdown;
  • [x] captioned images insert one escaped semantic figure fragment;
  • [x] preview and apply return identical source for the same request;
  • [x] fill-width images use the available column while natural-width images retain intrinsic width without overflowing;
  • [x] all three placements share one presentation component in Manage, public, and embedded-detail content;
  • [x] split layouts stack image-first at a narrow width;
  • [x] existing raster, SVG, Mermaid, collision, dirty-buffer, and file-link contracts remain working;
  • [x] no template files, format modal, arbitrary styling input, or generic fragment framework were introduced; and
  • [x] durable media and endpoint documentation describe only the shipped contract.

SIP-1 was accepted for delivery and closed on 2026-07-31. Representative manual acceptance covered the primary combinations rather than every possible control combination.
